title: Scientists Name a Giant Fungus “D-rex”
paragraphs: Researchers at the Kunming Institute of Botany in China have described a new fungus whose fruiting bodies, the visible mushroom-like parts, can reach about 50 centimetres in height and weigh up to 2.2 kilograms. They named it Dianjunus rex, nicknamed “D-rex”, and published the work in the journal Frontiers in Fungal Biology.

It grows on fallen wood and woody roots, often of Chinese cork oak trees, in forests in Yunnan Province. Within the large group Ascomycota, which has more than 64,000 known species, no other fungus has such tall fruiting bodies; the previous record holder reached 20 to 30 centimetres. Genetic tests suggest it belongs to a new family, Dianjunaceae, that appeared about 65 million years ago, shortly after the mass extinction that ended the age of the dinosaurs.

Some limits are important. The “largest” title applies only to Ascomycota, not to all fungi. The team also suggests that a tall body may help spread spores in dense forests, but this is a hypothesis, and large bodies cost a lot of energy to make.

questions.a: In forests in Yunnan Province, China.

questions.q: Which group does the size record apply to?

questions.a: No, it is only a hypothesis.
